label: <DEL> step of long sequences starting with b/g/w/a/j/v
explanation: Fires almost only on the <DEL> step (t == L), i.e. the step that outputs the first original token; it never fires in the copy phase and has only 6 tiny activations in the original phase. Within <DEL> steps, only 12.7% fire. Firing rate and magnitude go up sharply with sequence length (rate 0.2% at L=3-5 vs 16% at L=9; L>=8 holds 81% of mass) and with the identity of the first original token (b, g, w, a, j, v strongest, then e, n, i, o), with a weaker extra boost from the second token being in that same set. The top activations are L=8-9 sequences beginning b w/b j/w a. The response looks graded and distributed over token identities, not a sharp rule: the predicate gets 78% of mass but precision is only about 0.5. It does not fire on short sequences or on any copy-phase step.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: b, g, w, a, j, v; least: y, h, 1, x) and the next token to output (most: a, w, b, g, n, j; least: r, h, x, 1); timing cues that raise it most: phase=1, recall_idx=0, L=9 & t=9.
